name: overview
title: Device APIs and kernel APIs serve different needs
caption: Applications normally use native APIs. Optional POSIX compatibility covers selected OS services, not every peripheral contract.

name: languages
title: Language support and runtime support are separate
caption: The Rust row describes the inspected module, not every possible Rust port. All bindings still need valid C-side lifetimes and callback rules.

name: apis
title: A device pointer identifies an instance, not ownership
caption: Configuration, operations and mutable state have different jobs. Obtaining a device pointer does not grant exclusive access or prove readiness.

name: execution
title: A shared worker runs one handler at a time
caption: The ISR schedules work rather than running all application logic. The worker is one thread; other threads and interrupts can still execute.

name: memory
title: Object permission and RAM permission are different
caption: This illustrates a user-mode call that uses both a kernel object and a user buffer. Object authorization and buffer access are checked separately. Both applicable validations must succeed; their order is not prescribed here.

name: data-flow
title: Copying bytes, linking items and scheduling work differ
caption: These are three different mechanisms, not stages of one pipeline. A pointer copied by k_msgq still needs a referent-lifetime contract.

name: sensor-data
title: Fetch/Get and Read/Decode keep samples differently
caption: The upper path shares the driver cache. The lower path exposes a completed encoded buffer. Async behavior and supported operations remain driver-dependent.

name: lifecycle
title: Selection, readiness and shutdown are separate steps
caption: The build row summarizes static device startup. The work-item row requires a context that can wait safely; it is not a universal peripheral shutdown API.

name: debugging
title: Different tests expose different failures
caption: Test scopes are complementary, not a runtime pipeline. Zephyr bus emulation is prior art for stronger testing of nxrs’s existing providers, not a port target.

name: nxrs-lessons
title: Borrow explicit contracts, not another RTOS
caption: Apply these ideas inside nxrs’s Rust/NuttX design. Keep product configuration, lifetime and test requirements explicit without copying Zephyr’s build system.
